notes.title: Inventory system ~ Gem container 💎
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=RgaTx5CUA3c;full][/previewyoutube]

Hello again! Hope everyone is doing great. It's March already and autumn just arrived here in New Zealand! Another season, another Mahika update 💪

Been working hard getting the inventory system up and running, and the second part is now done and dusted. 👨‍🔧

We now have a working inventory layout and separated the inventory panel into 3 sections:
[list]
[*] Hotbar
[*] Item container and
[*] Gem container
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43049997/f179838cfb0fef07bb4d3e7fef95b7a1134afe78.png[/img]

Items that can be equipped will first try to go to the Hotbar. Then all gems go to the Gem container. And everything else that can't go to the Hotbar or Gem container will end up in the Item container if there are slots available.

Then, we repurposed the previously named "Gem panel" to become the "Magic panel".

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43049997/7ed32cefd8bb2d5efe66e86d5c2c1c77f699286a.png[/img]

This Magic panel will show the equipped gem at the bottom slot, then show the available magic at the other slots, and then equip the first tier magic when the gem is equipped.

The inventory can be accessed by pressing "i" in the keyboard. It will slide up and down including the Hotbar.

The Magic panel's hot keys, to equip magic and gem, were also re-mapped to make it closer to the default player movement keys.
[list]
[*] Q ~ 1st tier magic
[*] R ~ 2nd tier magic
[*] E ~ 3rd tier magic
[*] CTRL ~ Equip/Cycle between gems in the gem container
[/list]

Gems will be our main catalyst for magic. All magic will be available through gems.

Lastly, we fixed a bug that causes the cool down magic effect to reset when equipping a new gem.

That's it! More inventory system updates to come.

Thanks again for watching/reading the vlog/blog. We appreciate all your helpful feedback!

Stay safe and always have fun!

notes.title: First month update using Godot!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=IKsjffM-Y60;full][/previewyoutube]
Was a tough 1 month transition from Unity to Godot! Settled down now and have a better understanding on how Godot works ~ UI, Node structure, Lifecycle, GDScript!

YouTube tutorials, documentation and code samples really helped! This is what we've done so far with me doing 2-3 hours of after office game development using Godot 4.1.
[list]
[*] Character movement and animation now complete
[*] Character attack animation now complete
[*] Tilemap structure now complete with better understanding on how Godot arranges tiles and the features it provides
[*] Enemy simple chase player AI now complete
[/list]
Thanks to [url=https://www.facebook.com/dythrw]Dyethrow PIXEL[/url] for the awesome pixel art.
